That was an entertaining little last-wicket stand between Mohammed Siraj and Arshdeep Singh, but it shouldn't take away from how poorly India batted. These conditions were certainly not difficult enough to warrant being bowled out for just 209. The top order once again failed to deliver, with Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli falling to Matthew Fisher inside the first eight overs, the former's being a particularly soft dismissal. This was an ideal opportunity for Shreyas Iyer to silence his critics with a strong performance, but the right-hander once again fell prey to the short ball. Now, his vulnerability against the short ball remains a glaring concern. Axar Patel and Ishan Kishan both chipped in with 46, but neither could help India bat out their full 50 overs, with New Zealand's spinners taking care of the lower-middle order. Santner and Duffy finished with three wickets apiece, while Fisher struck twice early on to remove two big names from India's top order. New Zealand will fancy their chances of chasing this down and level the series. We will be back soon with the run chase..

[Reaching the milestone of 50 One-Day Internationals and reflecting on his journey through domestic cricket] I spent a lot of time playing domestic cricket, so it's nice to bring up that milestone in front of the home crowd. [Celebrating the milestone at Bay Oval with his family and receiving his commemorative silver jug] Yeah, it's great to come up here to the Mount. We stay in apartments here so the families can come along. So yeah, it's certainly cool to be sharing that milestone with them. And to have Lennox out there, he was, he was pretty excited. And I think he sang it pretty well as well. So it's very cool to see. [Emotions during the national anthem and sharing the occasion with his son Lennox] Yeah, absolutely. We spend a lot of time on the road. So whenever you can play here in New Zealand, it's really special. So yeah, it's cool to share that milestone. My grandma always used to say when we're watching the anthems that she used to get angry when people didn't sing. So make sure we sing nice and loud for her. And yeah, it's a cool moment to be out here. [Bowling performance of 1 for 35 and assessment of the conditions for spin] Yeah, I think it was a little bit there for the spin today. Second game on that wicket. So yeah, I think when I put the ball in a nice area, I was able to restrict them through the middle. And then the nasty fasties got some wickets as well. So it's a good all-round bowling performance. [Assessment of the pitch in his second match on the surface] Yeah, definitely looks like it's a little bit slower than the other night. So hopefully it cheers up a little bit later on and the scoring becomes a little bit easier.

Back in 2024, New Zealand brought an end to India's remarkable 12-year, 18-series unbeaten run in Test cricket at home. Now, India have returned the favour,  We are not suggesting that this carries the same magnitude as New Zealand's historic Test triumph, or that it will sting quite as much as India's defeat did back then, but it will certainly bring plenty of smiles to the Indian camp. Gautam Gambhir will be among those particularly pleased, having secured his first ODI series victory away from home as India's head coach. Interestingly, the last time New Zealand lost an ODI series at home was also against India, back in 2019.
